items.name: State machine: ORIENT through per-domain QUEUE
items.description: Implement advanceReverseEngineering for the per-domain analysis loop: ORIENT to SURVEY, SURVEY to GAP_ANALYSIS to DECOMPOSE to QUEUE, and the QUEUE advance (fixed path, first-vs-subsequent hash detection, schema/domain/path validation, parse) transitioning to the next domain's SURVEY or to the execution loop.
steps: Add case PhaseReverseEngineering to Advance() dispatch and create advanceReverseEngineering(s, in, dir).
Implement ORIENT->SURVEY (DomainIndex=1) and SURVEY->GAP_ANALYSIS->DECOMPOSE->QUEUE.

QUEUE: reject in.File; first advance reads <root>/.forgectl/state/reverse-engineering-queue.json, stores path+hash, validates (schema/domains/roots), parses into Queue; subsequent advance re-reads, rejects unchanged hash, else re-validates.
On valid QUEUE: if DomainIndex<DomainCount -> SURVEY (DomainIndex++), else -> EXECUTE_REVERSE_ENGINEER (ExecuteItemIndex=1) after rejecting an empty queue.

tests.description: ORIENT->SURVEY->GAP_ANALYSIS->DECOMPOSE->QUEUE advances in order; the first QUEUE advance reads the convention path, stores the hash, validates, and parses entries; a non-final domain returns to SURVEY with the index incremented while the final domain advances to EXECUTE_REVERSE_ENGINEER item 1.

A subsequent QUEUE advance whose file content changed recomputes the hash, re-validates, and advances.

items.name: State machine: per-item execution loop
items.description: Implement the EXECUTE_REVERSE_ENGINEER <-> POST_REVERSE_ENGINEER loop: reject an empty queue on entry, pre-create the domain specs/ directory (erroring with the path on failure), advance per item using depends_on-independent ordering, loop to the next item, exit to RECONCILE on the last item, and skip failed items silently. All paths resolve against the absolute project root, independent of cwd.
steps: On entering the loop with zero queue entries, return the 'Queue contains zero entries. Nothing to execute.' error and stay in EXECUTE_REVERSE_ENGINEER.
Before an item's action, ensure <root>/<domain>/specs/ exists (mkdir); if creation fails (permissions/disk), return an error naming the path.
Drive the loop by ExecuteItemIndex in stored queue order only; do NOT consult depends_on (Invariant 13: depends_on is RECONCILE metadata, ignored by the execution loop).
Each iteration concerns exactly the one queue entry's file (Invariant 6: single-file write per item); the transition mutates no other item's target.
EXECUTE->POST; POST increments ExecuteItemIndex and returns to EXECUTE while items remain, else transitions to RECONCILE (DomainIndex=1, ReconcileRound=1).
Take no failure path when an item produced no file (including when a code_search_roots directory was deleted after QUEUE validation).
Resolve the domain root and target file against the absolute project root (dir), never the current working directory.

tests.description: EXECUTE advances to POST; POST loops to EXECUTE with the item index incremented; POST on the last item advances to RECONCILE for domain 1 round 1; the domain specs/ directory is created before the item action is emitted.

The execution loop processes items strictly in stored queue order driven by ExecuteItemIndex and does not reorder by depends_on (Invariant 13), and each iteration targets only its own queue entry's file (Invariant 6).
Path resolution for the domain root and target file uses the absolute project root, so the loop behaves identically when forgectl is invoked from a directory outside the project (CWD portability).
Entering the execution loop with a zero-entry queue errors 'Queue contains zero entries. Nothing to execute.' and the state stays at EXECUTE_REVERSE_ENGINEER.
When the domain specs/ directory cannot be created (e.g. unwritable parent), EXECUTE returns an error naming the path.
An item that wrote no spec file still advances through POST with no error and no failure state.
A code_search_roots directory that existed at QUEUE time but was deleted before its EXECUTE item runs yields no spec file and the loop proceeds through POST to the next item without error.

items.name: State machine: per-domain reconcile loop
items.description: Implement RECONCILE -> RECONCILE_EVAL (verdict + min/max round bookkeeping), the optional COLLEAGUE_REVIEW gate, and RECONCILE_ADVANCE transitioning to the next domain or DONE. RECONCILE verifies that every spec file the queue expected for the domain exists, reporting any gap rather than fabricating a spec.
steps: On entering RECONCILE for a domain, verify each queue entry's target file for that domain exists on disk; if one is missing, report the gap (do not fabricate a spec).
RECONCILE->RECONCILE_EVAL.

RECONCILE_EVAL: append the verdict to the current domain's reconcile evals; FAIL & round<max -> RECONCILE (round++); PASS & round<min -> RECONCILE (round++); (PASS & round>=min) or (FAIL & round>=max) -> COLLEAGUE_REVIEW if ColleagueReview else RECONCILE_ADVANCE.
COLLEAGUE_REVIEW->RECONCILE_ADVANCE.
RECONCILE_ADVANCE: next domain -> RECONCILE (DomainIndex++, round=1); last domain -> DONE.

tests.description: With colleague_review disabled, a PASS at/after min_rounds advances RECONCILE_EVAL to RECONCILE_ADVANCE, which moves to the next domain's RECONCILE (round reset to 1) or to DONE on the last domain.

A FAIL below max_rounds and a PASS below min_rounds each return to RECONCILE with the round incremented; reaching max_rounds advances to COLLEAGUE_REVIEW when enabled or RECONCILE_ADVANCE when disabled regardless of verdict.
With colleague_review enabled, a passing RECONCILE_EVAL advances to COLLEAGUE_REVIEW which then advances to RECONCILE_ADVANCE.
When a spec file the queue expected for the domain is missing at RECONCILE, the gap is reported and no spec is fabricated.
